# Package types

This page is for administrators and developers who need to know what kind of package they hold. It answers: which
types exist, where the type is written, which types the package server offers, and what the type changes.

## Contents

1. [Where the type is declared](#where-the-type-is-declared)
2. [The types at a glance](#the-types-at-a-glance)
3. [The types in the 6.0.15 index](#the-types-in-the-6015-index)
4. [TypeList and what it is used for](#typelist-and-what-it-is-used-for)
5. [What the type changes](#what-the-type-changes)
6. [Type, install type and install items are three things](#type-install-type-and-install-items-are-three-things)
7. [Related pages](#related-pages)

## Where the type is declared

In two places, which must agree:

```xml
<!-- package.xml -->
<type value="site" />
```

```xml
<!-- index.xml on the package server -->
<package name="sevenx_multisite" version="6.0-15-stable" type="site" ... />
```

The kernel reads the value of `<type>` trimmed (`eZPackage::parseDOMTree()`), and refuses the definition when the
value is not a plain token of letters, digits and `._+-`. The setup wizard reads the `type` attribute of the index to
decide which remote packages are site packages (`eZStepSiteTypes::retrieveRemotePackagesList()`).

## The types at a glance

| Type | Holds | Made by | Typical install items | Examples |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `site` | A starter site: requirements and install scripts | by hand, in a source repository | none (`install_type="import"`) | `sevenx_multisite`, `cjw_multisite`, `plain_site` |
| `sitestyle` | A color scheme or design: CSS, images, thumbnail | the site style wizard (`ezstyle` creator) | `ezfile` | `sevenx_design_blue`, `ezflow_design` |
| `contentclass` | Content class definitions | the content class wizard (`ezcontentclass` creator) | `ezcontentclass` | `sevenx_classes`, `ezwebin_classes` |
| `contentobject` | Content, often with the classes it needs | the content object wizard, `ezpm add ... ezcontentobject` | `ezcontentobject`, sometimes `ezcontentclass` | `sevenx_multisite_democontent`, `sevenx_banners` |
| `extension` | One or more extensions as files | the extension export wizard (`ezextension` creator) | `ezextension` | `sevenx_extension`, `ezstarrating_extension` |

The creators and their package types are in `kernel/classes/packagecreators/*/` (`packageType()`), listed in
`settings/package.ini [CreationSettings] HandlerList[]`: `ezcontentobject`, `ezcontentclass`, `ezextension`,
`ezstyle`.

> **Note**
> There is no package type `design`. Design files travel in `sitestyle` packages, or inside an extension. The word
> `design` does appear in `package.xml`, but as the type of a `<file-list>` (files that go below
> `design/<design>/`), not as a package type.

## The types in the 6.0.15 index

The 44 entries of `https://exponential.packages.exponential.earth/exponential/6.0/6.0.15/index.xml`, counted by
their `type` attribute:

| Type | Entries |
|---|---|
| `site` | 12 |
| `contentobject` | 13 |
| `extension` | 8 |
| `sitestyle` | 7 |
| `contentclass` | 4 |

The index groups the non-site packages under the comment `DEPENDENCY PACKAGE LIST`: they are offered only as
requirements of a site package, never as a choice of their own. The complete list is in
[What is on the package server](../package-server/what-is-on-the-package-server.md).

## TypeList and what it is used for

```ini
[PackageSettings]
TypeList[]
TypeList[contentobject]=Content object
TypeList[contentclass]=Content class
TypeList[sitestyle]=Site style
TypeList[site]=Site
TypeList[extension]=Extension
```

`eZPackage::typeList()` turns this into the list of types with their names. Its main use is the **Type
limitation** of the package policies: `kernel/package/module.php` gives the functions `read`, `list`, `create`,
`edit`, `remove`, `install`, `import` and `export` a limitation `Type` whose values come from `typeList()`. A user
whose policy is limited by Type may use a package only when its type is among the chosen values
(`eZPackage::canUsePackagePolicyFunction()`).

> **Note**
> `extension` is in `TypeList` from 6.0.15 on. Before, it was missing, so a Type limitation could not name it and a
> role limited by Type never reached packages of type `extension`. On an older release, add it in
> `settings/override/package.ini.append.php`:
>
> ```ini
> [PackageSettings]
> TypeList[extension]=Extension
> ```

## What the type changes

| Where | What the type does |
|---|---|
| Setup wizard, Site types step | Only `site` packages are offered, local (`fetchPackages()` with `'type' => 'site'`) and remote (`type="site"` in the index) |
| Create sites step | Nothing: it installs what the site package requires, whatever their types |
| Package policies | The Type limitation (above) |
| Package list in the administration | Shown on each card; the list can be filtered by type in `eZPackage::fetchPackages()` |
| Install | Nothing: `install()` looks at `install_type` and the install items, never at the type |

## Type, install type and install items are three things

| | Says | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `<type value>` | What the package is | `sitestyle` |
| `install_type` | Whether `install()` runs the items at all | `import` |
| `<install><item type>` | Which handler does the work for one item | `ezfile` |

A `sitestyle` package of 7x is type `sitestyle`, install type `import`, with one `ezfile` item: it is imported so
the site package's installer can use its files, and installing it on its own changes nothing. See
[Import versus install](import-versus-install.md) and [Install items and handlers](install-items-and-handlers.md).
